messages.author: 56e0e5c14f030fcf
messages.subject: censored dynamic linear model
parts:
i'm using Rstan and trying to write a model for doing dynamic linear model with right censoring, basically a simple state-space model with poisson likelihood. I run into the issue of 

[1] "Error : Rejecting initial value:"                                                                     
  [2] "  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity."                                       
  [3] "  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value."   

not sure where i did wrong ... here's the relevant code.


data {
  int<lower = 1> N;                           // number of observations
  int<lower = 0> y[N];                       // count time series
  int<lower = 0, upper = 1> flag[N];  // censoring indicator, i.e., whether the true value >= the observation. 
}

parameters {
...
vector[N] u; // latent process
...
}

model {
...

for (t in 2:N) {
  u[t] ~ normal(f(u[t-1]), sigma) 

  if (flag[t] == 1) {
     increment_log_prob(poisson_ccdf_log(y[t], exp(u[t])));  // right censoring
  } else {
    increment_log_prob(poisson_log_log(y[t], u[t])); 
 }
}

removing the right censoring line runs, but it just means ignoring the partial observations. Any hints will be appreciated. 

Best,
Bernie

us if we don't have to guess the missing bits.

The error you're getting is because the initial state isn't
valid. So you need to trace through it to find out what's going
wrong. You can use print() statements.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] censored dynamic linear model
parts:
Yes, I mean printing out arguments and results of applying functions
to make sure everything has the values you expect.

Also, you don't need that truncation on the Cauchy.
It comes for free with the declaration <lower=0> and
the fact that the parameters to the Cauchy are constant
and we only need the log density up to an additive constant.

You also define l to be of size N, but only use (N-1) values.

There are lots of optimizations you can then do once this
is working to precompute the branches due to flag (which I'd
call "is_censored[N]" rather than "flag[N]".

- Bob

parts:
found the issue with print. Thanks!

the reason was that the counts are high but the estimated log rate is low, resulting in 0's from ccdf and thus giving -inf for log(ccdf). 

on a separate note, i had to mute

// increment_log_prob(poisson_ccdf_log(y[t], exp(u[t])));  // right censoring

in

print(poisson_ccdf_log(y[t], exp(u[t]))
increment_log_prob(poisson_ccdf_log(y[t], exp(u[t])));  // right censoring

otherwise, nothing gets printed out. 

Bernie
